title: Choose the layout
question: Three ways to arrange the analyzer in the index-card style. Pick the one you want built, or re-roll for others.

options.label: Profile rail
options.thesis: Your skills live in a permanent left rail, like a card box you keep across postings.
options.viewport: Left rail: skill cards with how many requirements each covers. Main: collapsed posting strip, then divider-tabbed rows of cards for gaps, not listed, and matched.
options.risk: The posting is tucked into a strip, so editing it is one click away instead of always visible.

options.label: Marked-up posting
options.thesis: The posting itself becomes the result: every skill it mentions is highlighted in its status colour, like a printout gone over with highlighters.
options.viewport: Skills as a chip bar under the header. Left: the posting on a ruled sheet with highlighted mentions. Right: the result cards, the selected mention's card enlarged.
options.risk: Strongest for evidence, but long postings push results off-screen on phones; needs a careful mobile layout.

options.label: Three steps
options.thesis: Posting, then skills, then results, one screen at a time, with results laid out as three side-by-side card stacks.
options.viewport: Step bar under the header (Posting, Your skills, Results). Results step: posting title and summary, then three columns: gaps, not in profile, matched.
options.risk: Clearest for first use, but slower when iterating: changing a skill means stepping back.
